short: The long first chapter of human technology, defined by chipped stone tools and a foraging way of life.
full:
The Palaeolithic, or Old Stone Age, covers roughly 99% of human technological history. It opens with the earliest known deliberately struck stone tools, found at Lomekwi in Kenya and dated to about 3.3 million years ago — predating our own genus. Over that immense span, toolmaking traditions moved from simple flakes and choppers to the finely worked blades, bone points and needles of the Upper Palaeolithic.

People lived in small mobile groups, hunting and gathering, following herds and seasons. The period also contains the first unambiguous evidence of symbolic life: burials with grave goods, personal ornament, and the cave art of Chauvet, Lascaux and Altamira. It ends with the retreat of the last glaciation, around 12,000 BCE, as a warming climate reorganised the ecosystems people depended on.
